title: Product Launch Video and Photos for New Drops | AIVideosUGC
description: Plan product launch videos and photos: teaser clips before the drop, a reveal video on launch day, and product-page scenes for each milestone after it.
h1: Product Launch Video and Photos, Ready Before Launch Day
lead: Plan teaser clips, a reveal video, and product-page photos around each launch milestone, with final dates and prices added after download.
card: Teasers, a reveal clip and product page photos from your first sample shot.
intro: A launch can call for a teaser, a reveal, product-page photos, and a follow-up post. List the placements and visual stages before choosing which assets to prepare.

If you have a photo of a sample, use it to make launch clips and product photos. If you do not have a product photo yet, you can start a video with a written description; every product photo requires an uploaded photo. Add the launch date, price, and product name after download in Canva or CapCut.

faq.q: Can I make launch content before my product is finished?
faq.a: A video can start from a written description alone. Every product photo requires one uploaded photo, such as a clear image of a sample or prototype.

faq.q: Can I change launch details after making a video?
faq.a: Yes. Add the date, price, or code as editable text after download so you can update confirmed details without regenerating the scene.

faq.q: Will anyone see my unreleased product before I announce it?
faq.a: No. Your uploads and the results stay in your own account and are never made public, so the product stays under wraps until you share it.

faq.q: What video size should a product launch use?
faq.a: Use 9:16 for Stories, Reels, and TikTok; 1:1 for feeds; and 16:9 for a wide product page or YouTube placement. Make each size as its own job.

overview.h2: Give every launch asset one job
overview.d: A teaser creates curiosity by withholding part of the product. A reveal identifies the item and shows its shape. A product-page image answers a buying question. Plan those jobs separately so the launch set does not repeat one pretty scene six times. If your sample changes before release, regenerate the visual from the newest photo and compare every result with the item customers will actually receive.

overview.h2: Prepare the visual before the wording is final
overview.d: AIVideosUGC offers five video shapes—9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, and 3:4—and 6, 10, 15, and 30 second jobs; each credit cost appears before generation. Make the scene while the launch wording is still changing, then add the exact name, price, date, code, and availability in Canva, CapCut, or your publishing tool. Uploaded source photos and generated drafts remain inside your account until you choose to download and share them.

input_guide.h2: Start with the sample customers will recognize

items.d: Use a clear view of the prototype or sample, including the parts that are likely to remain in the shipped product.
For a teaser, name the material, edge, or silhouette you want to hint at; do not rely on generated text to hide the product cleanly.
Say whether the item turns, opens, slides from a box, or settles into its use setting. One reveal action is easier to review.

results.h2: A launch set that moves from hint to proof

items.d: A partial view or material detail that earns a second look without making a claim about demand.
A complete product view in a video crop or square still chosen for the channel where you will announce it.
A clean still or lifestyle frame that lets a shopper inspect the item after the announcement.

scene_recipes.h2: Launch scenes for one new product

items.d: A close view of a matte bottle shoulder catches a narrow beam of light while the full shape stays just outside the frame.
A plain shipping box opens on a table and the new product is lifted into the center against a calm background.
A hand places the product in the room where it belongs, showing one real use without a testimonial or invented result.
The packed product rests beside tissue paper and an insert card, with the actual contents visible for review.

after_download.h2: Lock the launch details in your editor

items.d: Type the product name, date, price, and availability yourself, then check every character against the launch plan.
Compare color, parts, packaging, and proportions with the sample that will ship. Regenerate a scene that changes a meaningful detail.
For video, use 9:16 for phone-first placements, 1:1 for square feeds, or 16:9 for a wide page when the composition benefits from it.
Download only when the launch team is ready to share; the source and generated work stay in your account before that point.

fit.h2: A good fit for staged launches
good: Products with a photographed prototype or sample
Launches that need distinct teaser, reveal, and listing scenes
Teams whose launch dates and offer details may change during preparation
Sellers willing to inspect every generated detail against the final item
not_ideal: Products whose final form is still unknown
Announcements that depend on AI-generated prices, dates, or technical labels

visual.overview: Plan a product launch from a clear sample photo, with separate scenes for packaging, first use, and the store listing.

steps.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the only product reference. Preserve its matte turquoise bottle, cap, proportions and finish. In a bright launch-day kitchen, an adult lifts the bottle for one sip and holds it beside their face. Natural phone-shot UGC in soft window light. Chest-up framing with one gentle push-in; end with the bottle clear beside the face. Sound: a quiet sip and room tone; no music or added text.
